spec.description: CPU-only BLIP captioning app (Streamlit) monitored with Prometheus + node_exporter.

spec.title: Throughput — images captioned per second
spec.description: Per-second rate of the images counter (1-minute window). Bulk ZIPs produce a sustained plateau; single uploads produce short blips. Failed images shown separately. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Requests per minute by mode
spec.description: How often users submit work: one request = one Single upload or one whole ZIP. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Totals since app start
spec.description: Raw counter values (reset when the app restarts).

spec.title: Inference latency percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99)
spec.description: From the inference histogram: 95% of images finished faster than the p95 line. A widening gap between p50 and p99 means inconsistent latency (e.g. CPU contention). X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Average time per image (Summary _sum / _count)
spec.description: Mean end-to-end seconds per image, by mode, from the Summary metric, plus the preprocessing share. Gaps = no traffic in that window (0/0). X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Inference latency distribution (heatmap)
spec.description: Each column = 1 minute; each cell = how many images fell in that latency bucket. Brighter (yellow) = more images. Viridis colour scale is colour-blind safe. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

yAxis.axisLabel: Latency bucket upper bound, s (ordinal buckets)

spec.title: In-flight work
spec.description: Gauges: requests being processed right now, and images still waiting in the current bulk job (counts down to 0 as a ZIP is processed). X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Skipped files in ZIPs (by reason)
spec.description: Non-image, hidden/system, oversized or over-limit files ignored during Bulk mode. Empty = none skipped.

options.content:
**Top → bottom = high-level → low-level**

1 Health · 2 Traffic · 3 Latency · 4 Workload & clients · 5 App ↔ hardware correlation · 6–7 System resources

Colours use the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette; series also differ by line style (solid / dashed / dotted). Every time-series x-axis is wall-clock time. Hover the ⓘ icon on any panel for its story. Red markers = firing alerts.

spec.title: Errors (by mode · type)
spec.description: Exceptions caught by the app, e.g. BadZipFile for a corrupt ZIP. Empty = no errors.

spec.title: Requests by client (custom labels)
spec.description: Client metadata attached as labels on caption_requests_total: session ID, source IP, browser.

spec.title: Throughput vs host CPU
spec.description: Left axis: images/sec (solid). Right axis: host CPU % (dashed). During a bulk upload both rise together — proof that inference is the CPU consumer. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: CPU cores used: app process vs whole host
spec.description: Both in cores. When the app line nearly matches the host line, the captioning app is responsible for almost all CPU load. Top line = cores available. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Memory: app process vs host
spec.description: App RSS jumps when the model loads (~1.7 GB) and stays there — the model stays resident and Python keeps memory it has allocated. Host used includes the OS and other tools. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: CPU utilisation by mode
spec.description: user = application code (PyTorch inference), system = kernel, iowait = waiting on disk. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Memory & swap used %
spec.description: If RAM nears 100% and swap starts rising, the VM is under memory pressure and inference slows. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: System load average vs cores
spec.description: Load = runnable tasks. Load above the cores line means work is queueing for CPU. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: App status
spec.description: Can Prometheus scrape the captioning app (:8000)? UP = last scrape succeeded. If DOWN, every application panel below goes flat.

spec.title: Disk I/O throughput
spec.description: Bytes/sec read and written across real disks (loop and CD-ROM devices excluded by regex). X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Disk space used (/)
spec.description: Root filesystem usage. Model weights, Prometheus data and Docker images all live here. X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: Network throughput
spec.description: Bytes/sec on real interfaces (loopback and Docker virtual interfaces excluded by regex). X-axis: wall-clock time (browser timezone).

spec.title: node_exporter status
spec.description: Can Prometheus scrape node_exporter (:9100)? Needed for all system panels.

spec.title: Model
spec.description: LOADED = BLIP weights are in RAM and warmed up, so the app can serve requests.

spec.title: Firing alerts
spec.description: Number of Prometheus alert rules currently firing (also sent to Alertmanager).

spec.title: App uptime
spec.description: Time since the Streamlit process started. Counters reset when it restarts.

spec.title: Since last caption
spec.description: Seconds since the last successful caption. Grows while the app is idle.
